summary: Create Runtime-ops cross-team collaboration space: Confluence space, Jira alert-driven project, and ephemeral Slack bridges
description:
Issue summary:
We need a lightweight cross-team collaboration workspace for the Runtime Ops team to coordinate alerts, postmortems, and short-lived incident channels. The deliverable is a Confluence space with templated pages and permission groups, a dedicated Jira project with an automation rule that creates and tags issues from incoming alert webhooks, and an ephemeral Slack channel pattern with an approval + archiver bot to create short-lived bridges for on-call rotations.

Impact:
- Current alerts are routed to ad-hoc channels and personal DMs which causes knowledge fragmentation and slow incident kickoff.
- Lack of templated postmortem pages means missing structured RCA artifacts.

Background context:
- Runtime Ops (multi-pod SRE + Serving infra) will use this workspace for high-frequency low-severity alerts and to coordinate cross-pod escalations into Dedicated/Private platform teams.
- The workspace should support: role-based access (SRE, Platform, Security), read-only view for Managers, and ephemeral write access for incident participants.

Requested work items (deliverables):
1) Confluence: create space "Runtime Ops - Incidents & Alerts" with templates: Incident triage, Postmortem, Runbook change request. Set permissions: space-admins = group:runtime-ops-admins, editors = group:runtime-ops-oncall, viewers = group:eng-leads. Create one namespace page for archival policy referencing legal retention (link below).
2) Jira: create project key ROT (Runtime Ops Tickets) with issue types: Alert, Incident, Postmortem Task. Add Jira automation rule: when webhook /api/alerts creates an Alert issue, set labels based on severity, auto-assign to oncall rotation based on schedule, and create linked Postmortem Task if severity >= Sev2.
3) Slack: provision private channel pattern #rot-<rotation>-<YYYYMMDD>-ephemeral created via bot. The channel must allow a 72-hour auto-archive unless extended by space-admins. Add a bridge bot that can archive the channel by running /rot-archive and post a summary link to the Confluence incident page.
4) Integrations & Automation: provide a sample GitHub Action or Terraform snippet for the alerting webhook and an Ops repo PR template that references the new ROT project. Provide minimal runbook for oncall to create channels and connect them to Jira issues.

Acceptance criteria (see separate field): space exists, Jira project created, automation tested with sample webhook, Slack ephemeral flow demoed in staging, permission groups configured and documented.

Notes and constraints:
- Security has requested that all space-admins be SSO-mapped groups and that Confluence pages containing PII be restricted. No PII will be stored in default templates.
- We prefer to use existing group names where possible to reduce manual provisioning work.

References:
- Slack policy: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/SEC/Slack+Channel+Policies
- Legal retention notes: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/LEGAL/Record+Retention
acceptance_criteria: Confluence space 'Runtime Ops - Incidents & Alerts' exists and is reachable with templated pages for Incident, Postmortem, and Runbook changes
Jira project ROT created with Alert and Incident issue types and automation rule that accepts webhook payloads and creates linked Postmortem tasks for severity >= Sev2
Slack ephemeral channel creation + archive flow works in staging: bot creates #rot-<rotation>-<date>-ephemeral, can archive via /rot-archive, and posts Confluence link on archive
Permission groups (runtime-ops-admins, runtime-ops-oncall) mapped to SSO groups and documented in the Confluence space
Integration examples (Terraform / GH Action) and a short runbook are added to the Confluence space

investigation_notes:
Feasibility check performed:
- Confluence: OK to create a new space; templates can use variables and page properties for metadata. Will add data_classification property and an 'archival_date' field.
- Jira: Recommend new project key ROT to avoid collision. Jira automation supports webhook trigger and conditional create. Oncall assignment will pull from OpsSchedule via a small lambda that returns user mapping.
- Slack: Existing bot 'channel-orchestrator' supports temporary channels; needs a minor permission grant to auto-archive and to post to Confluence.
- Timelines: Estimated 3 business days to create spaces and templates, 2 days to implement Jira automation and webhook lambda, 1 day to wire Slack bot in staging and demo. Total ~6 business days if approvals are fast.
- Risks: SSO group mapping could take time if new groups need provisioning; Legal review on retention could add delay.
implementation_steps: 1) Create Confluence space skeleton and add templates; set space-admins = runtime-ops-admins
2) Create Jira project ROT; configure issue types and workflow for Alert -> Triage -> Incident
3) Implement Jira Automation rule: webhook -> create Alert -> set labels/priority -> link Postmortem Task when severity >= Sev2
4) Deploy small lambda to translate alert payloads to Jira webhook and to look up OpsSchedule for oncall assignee
5) Update and grant permissions to Slack 'channel-orchestrator' bot; test ephemeral channel creation and auto-archive in staging
6) Document runbook and add integration snippets to Confluence; request security/legal signoff on templates
7) Demo to Runtime Ops team and collect feedback; roll to prod after signoff
resolution: Pending - awaiting Security and Legal approvals for Confluence templates and TTL policy. Implementation scheduled to begin after approvals.
